raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not toss money around. On 6 mu, if I make a big mistake, it hurts the whole family. What I usually do is still wheat and maize on the same land. That is the steady way here in Quzhou. I watch what the neighbors do, and I keep close to what has worked on my fields. We have a well, so if the weather turns dry I can still save the crop, but pumping costs money, so I will not water too many times unless the field really needs it.

For wheat, I do not chase the very highest yield. I put a fair base fertilizer before sowing, then one more urea topdressing when the wheat is growing up strong in spring. If the leaves stay green and the stand looks even, I do not keep adding more. For maize after wheat, the turnaround is tight, so I want quick harvest of wheat, simple rotary tillage or even just light preparation, then sow maize right away. I will buy hybrid maize seed because saved maize seed is not reliable. If rain is normal, one irrigation for maize may be enough; if summer is dry, I will add one more. Since some family members work outside, I keep the plan simple and use machine services where needed.
